terms.label: Affine hull of a set of vectors
Mutually independent indexed family of events
Pairwise independent indexed family of events

observations.text: On the real space R^d, the affine hull of S comprises finite sums of points of S with real coefficients whose total is exactly one; with S empty, no such combination exists.
observations.editorial_note: Harvard-hosted mathematical background §1.2.1, finite-dimensional R^n and explicit empty-hull convention; independently rewritten.

observations.text: The affine hull is the least affine-closed set containing S, equivalently the intersection of all affine-closed supersets of S. Empty S has empty affine hull under the affine-closed-set convention.
observations.editorial_note: Harvard §1.2.1 states smallest affine subspace and the empty-set convention; 'affine-closed' makes the empty convention explicit.

observations.text: Two measurable events are independent when the probability of their intersection equals the product of their probabilities. The product formula is meaningful even if either event has probability zero.
observations.editorial_note: ProofWiki main page Definition 2 uses a positive-probability preamble, but its general finite-family definition does not; the pair product-law extension to zero probability is valid.

observations.text: An indexed family of measurable events is jointly independent if all its finite subfamilies have intersection probabilities equal to the product of the event probabilities.
observations.editorial_note: ProofWiki general definition quantified over all finite index subsets, not just pairs; empty index subset works by P(Omega)=1.

observations.text: An indexed family of events is pairwise independent when the two-event probability product rule holds for each pair with distinct indices.
observations.editorial_note: ProofWiki explicitly equates the condition with all size-two index subsets, but its symbolic quantifier omits j≠k. Correct distinct-index interpretation adopted; source defect logged as issue.

observations.text: A cycle in a simple loopless undirected graph can be represented by at least three distinct vertices in cyclic order, with an edge between each consecutive pair including last to first.
observations.editorial_note: ProofWiki's broad circuit/cycle definition allows other graph types and flags the ≥3 restriction for simple graphs; only simple undirected context is admitted here.

meanings.context: Finite-dimensional real affine geometry: subsets of R^d, integer d≥1, with empty hull allowed

formulations.text: For an integer d≥1 and a set S⊆ℝ^d, aff(S) is the set of all vectors ∑_{i=1}^{k} αᵢxᵢ with k≥1, xᵢ∈S, αᵢ∈ℝ and ∑_{i=1}^{k} αᵢ=1. In particular aff(∅)=∅.
formulations.mathematical_rationale: The real coefficient-sum-one requirement is essential and differs from convex combinations, which require nonnegative coefficients; allowing arbitrary finite k but k≥1 makes the empty-set case exactly ∅.

formulations.text: Let d≥1 and S⊆ℝ^d. Define aff(S) as the intersection of all affine-closed subsets C⊆ℝ^d containing S, where affine-closed means containing every finite affine combination of its members; the empty set is affine-closed.
formulations.mathematical_rationale: The intersection characterization is source-backed and equivalent to the finite-combination characterization, explicitly allowing the empty affine-closed set so aff(∅)=∅ without a nonempty affine-subspace convention conflict.

meanings.context: Probability theory: two measurable events in a probability space, including probability-zero cases

formulations.text: For measurable A,B in a probability space (Ω,Σ,P), the events A and B are independent if and only if P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B). No positive-probability assumption is required for this product-rule definition.
formulations.mathematical_rationale: The source's unconditional product identity, interpreted via the general independent-family definition, remains valid for P(A)=0 or P(B)=0; conditional-probability formulations need separate nonzero-denominator hypotheses.

meanings.context: Probability theory: joint independence of an arbitrary indexed family of measurable events

formulations.text: For a probability space (Ω,Σ,P) and indexed measurable events (Aᵢ)_{i∈I}, the family is mutually independent if for every finite J⊆I, P(⋂_{j∈J} Aⱼ)=∏_{j∈J}P(Aⱼ), with the empty intersection Ω and empty product 1.
formulations.mathematical_rationale: Every finite index subset is required, not merely every size-two subset; under the empty-index convention both sides equal 1, and repeated equal events at different indices still count as distinct indexed entries.

meanings.context: Probability theory: pairwise but not necessarily jointly independent indexed measurable events

formulations.text: Let (Aᵢ)_{i∈I} be measurable events on one probability space. The family is pairwise independent if for every i,j∈I with i≠j, P(Aᵢ∩Aⱼ)=P(Aᵢ)P(Aⱼ). This does not in general imply joint independence for three or more events.
formulations.mathematical_rationale: Distinct indices are required, because allowing i=j forces P(Aᵢ)=P(Aᵢ)² and wrongly excludes nontrivial event probabilities; ProofWiki's cardinality-two restatement supports the distinct-index reading despite a displayed quantifier omission.

meanings.display_term: cycle in a simple undirected graph
meanings.context: Graph theory: a finite cycle in a loopless simple undirected graph; length at least three

formulations.text: For a simple loopless undirected graph G=(V,E), a cycle is a finite cyclic sequence v₀,v₁,…,v_{k−1},v₀ with k≥3, the vertices v₀,…,v_{k−1} pairwise distinct, and {vᵢ,v_{(i+1) mod k}}∈E for every 0≤i<k.
formulations.mathematical_rationale: The source's circuit-with-no-repeated-intermediate-vertex definition specializes to simple undirected loopless graphs; k≥3 excludes loops and length-two parallel-edge cycles allowed by broader multigraph conventions.

relations.target_query: Affine combination of finitely many vectors in a real vector space
relations.editorial_reason: Affine hull construction requires the independently sourced notion of a finite affine combination with coefficients summing to one, distinct from convex combinations.
The affine-closed superset characterization is scoped to a real vector space; the existing field-vector-space definition provides the structural ambient addition and scalar multiplication.
The pairwise probability identity presupposes a normalized probability space and measurable events; this is an independently screened matching probability-space meaning.
The finite-family intersection and probability product must be evaluated with a single probability measure on the measurable event space.
Pairwise independence reduces to the previously defined independent-event condition for every two DISTINCT indices, not to the stronger all-finite-subfamilies condition.
An undirected cycle uses edges as two-element vertex subsets, excluding loops and parallel edges; the independently screened loopless simple-graph context matches precisely.
